clue.text: Pope detailed universal language to win over citizens

indicators.note: de-tailed: the word Pope loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its tail is cut
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: to win something is to take it in, so the language holds the next piece

parts.note: Latin is a language
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: The Pope speaks Latin to charm the faithful of his city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as de-tailed, cutting a last letter; 'to win' means take in. 'over' is the cricket term, six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A population is the whole body of people living in a place, its inhabitants collectively.

clue.text: Seeking alternatives to opium? Best try here!

definitions.text: Seeking alternatives to opium? Best try here!

indicators.note: alternatives here means alternate letters, every other one, taken from these words

explanation.surface: Advice to someone giving up opium: a better escape can be found elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'oPiUm' and 'BeSt'. The whole clue also defines: Marx called religion the opium of the people, and a bar offers another comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars serving alcohol are where someone wanting a different intoxicant might go instead.

clue.text: Mate brought round five eggs for dessert

indicators.note: the friend is brought round the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
V is the Roman numeral for five
ova are eggs, the Latin plural

explanation.surface: A friend comes over with five eggs to make a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' puts V inside PAL to give PAVL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavlova is a meringue pudding topped with cream and fruit, named after a ballerina.

clue.text: Used clothes store?

parts.note: not a second-hand shop: worn clothes waiting for the wash are stored in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Used clothes store' suggests a charity shop selling second-hand clothes; 'store' is a verb or container, and 'used' means worn and dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: This household container holds dirty clothing until wash day, so it stores worn garments.

clue.text: Detective shot in the arm, causing upheavals?

parts.note: tec is old slang for a detective
a shot in the arm is a boost, a tonic

explanation.surface: A policeman injected in the arm reacts with violent convulsions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by description: tectonic forces raise mountains and cause earthquakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tectonic plate movements heave up the Earth's crust, so the adjective fits upheavals.

clue.text: The deep loch meant banks repeatedly eroded

indicators.note: the banks are each word's outer letters, worn away from both words in turn

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake whose shores keep being worn away by water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks repeatedly eroded' strips the outside letters of 'lOCh' and 'mEANt'.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic name for the sea, the open water far from land.

clue.text: Creature one's tracking already

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: yet can mean already, as in 'Has he come yet?'
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Some animal has been following our trail for a while already.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracking' puts I after YET.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the legendary abominable snowman, a creature said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Implicate Republican in mobile getting hacked

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the jumbled word
hacked means chopped up, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is implicated after his mobile phone is hacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked' reorders MOBILE as EMBOIL; 'in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to involve them in a conflict or difficulty, to implicate them.

clue.text: Plastic skis create cool slippers?

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so these letters can be reshaped

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Skis made of plastic produce footwear that is cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool slippers' are not footwear: the question mark marks people who slip on cold ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Skaters glide, or slip, across frozen water, so the phrase is a playful description.

clue.text: In Cuba, dancing, ten going round very camp

indicators.note: the scrambled word has the other pieces set in it
dancing letters move about, so the word Cuba is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the figures for ten wrap around the next letter

parts.note: 10 written as letters looks like IO

explanation.surface: Out dancing in Cuba, someone counts ten and circles a very camp scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' is the digits 1 and 0 written as letters. 'dancing' scrambles the island's name; 'going round' and 'In' are both containers, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivouac is a temporary camp, especially one without tents, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Raise children — no blessings at heart?

indicators.note: at heart means the letters sit in the middle of these words, hidden in them

explanation.surface: Bringing up children with no blessings at all, a gloomy family scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'childrEN NO BLEssings'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, or figuratively to elevate them.

clue.text: Outfit for country house visits

parts.note: not clothing but an organisation: outfit means a body or group

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' suggests clothes to wear on a stately-home trip; it is the organisation. The National Trust is the British charity that runs historic houses for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: This British charity owns and opens many stately homes, so it is the body behind such visits.

clue.text: Steam railway, say, visited by gracious ruling elite

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so the exclamation is put inside

parts.note: a steam railway is an example of an old network of lines
'Gracious!' and 'Boy!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A heritage steam line receives a visit from gracious members of the governing class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' is the exclamation 'Gracious!', matched by 'Boy!'; 'visited by' is the container. 'say' marks a steam railway as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The old boy network is the informal web of influence among former pupils of elite schools who hold power.

clue.text: Love new filling cooked in oil vessel

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the letter is put into the cooking word

parts.note: food cooked in oil is fried
a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: A kitchen tale: a new filling fried in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts N inside FRIED to give FRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendship is affection between people, a kind of love, so it fits loosely as a synonym.

clue.text: Study variables limiting motorway type of concrete

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, especially at university

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so the variables go around the road

parts.note: x and y are the usual algebraic variables
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, so MI

explanation.surface: A research note on variables restricting motorway building materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' puts MI (the M1, London to Leeds motorway) between Y and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-mix concrete is delivered already mixed to the site, a kind of building material.

clue.text: Slough, making comeback, agree to appearing in cup

indicators.note: coming back means the word for slough is read from right to left

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog
to let something happen is to agree to it

explanation.surface: Slough's football club stages a comeback and agrees to play in the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns BOG into GOB. Slough is also an English town, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a drinking cup with a stem and base, so it is a type of cup.

clue.text: Chill out, beginning with stupendous dope

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

parts.note: dope is slang for inside information, the lowdown

explanation.surface: Advice to relax, starting with some amazing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs; here it is information.
explanation.definitionFit: To slow down is to relax and take things more easily, as chilling out is.

clue.text: Ignoring outside right, fellow striker maybe shoots over net

indicators.note: shooting over means flipping back, so the word is read in reverse
ignoring something means leaving it out, here a letter

parts.note: a striker's strike partner is a fellow forward
the R on the outside, the end, of the word; also a football wing position

explanation.surface: A forward ignores the winger, and his strike partner fires over the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring' drops the outer R from PARTNER to leave PARTNE; 'shoots over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a creature is to catch it, which is to trap it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Its application offers a firm digital protection

definitions.text: Its application offers a firm digital protection

parts.words: Its application offers a firm digital protection
parts.note: not computer security: digital means of the finger, and it is a firm sewing cap

explanation.walkthrough: 'digital protection' points at cyber security; 'digital' means of the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is a hard cap worn on a fingertip when sewing to guard it from the needle.

clue.text: Nitrogen needed in cereals, rum and soap

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A recipe list: fertiliser for cereals, a bottle of rum and some soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the old British slang for odd, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is a substance used for washing, which is what a cleanser is.

clue.text: Gush over theatre star

parts.note: a surge is a sudden gush of water or feeling
on can mean over, on top of

explanation.surface: Fans gush over a star of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is the leading figure in a hospital operating theatre, its star performer.

clue.text: Clean liquid below a terrace is doing this!

parts.words: below a terrace is doing this
parts.note: the words 'beloW A TERrace' hold the five letters of the drink inside them, so the phrase is literally taking it in

explanation.surface: A notice under a garden terrace announcing that the tap water there is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'drinking' means containing, and the phrase 'beloW A TERrace' contains WATER. That is what 'is doing this' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Water fit for people to drink is clean, safe, potable liquid.

clue.text: Score part for piano — Tchaikovsky …

indicators.note: the letters form a part of these words, hidden across them

explanation.surface: A score with a piano part, written by Tchaikovsky, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'piaNO TCHaikovsky'. Score here is a cut, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut a mark into it, which is a notch.

clue.text: .. calls it 'Overture for Revolution' — featuring American singer

indicators.note: for Revolution says the hidden letters are read backwards
featuring means containing, so the words hold the singer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tchaikovsky names his piece 'Overture for Revolution', starring an American vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'featuring', which cannot stand for a name; 'featuring' signals the hidden letters SITO in 'calLS IT Overture', reversed by 'for Revolution'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otis Redding was a celebrated American soul singer, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Uniform former volunteers displayed around home

parts.note: a habit is the uniform dress of a monk or nun

indicators.note: turned around means the letters run backwards

parts.note: the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, now renamed

explanation.surface: A uniform worn by ex-reservists is on show around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed around' is the reversal; 'former' because the Territorial Army was renamed the Army Reserve in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural place where an animal or plant lives, its home.

clue.text: Work you, by text, provided for rich

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
in text-message spelling, you is written U
to provide money for a time is to lend it

explanation.surface: A business message: the work you texted about is provided for the wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes great wealth and luxury, so it is a synonym of rich.

clue.text: Spy's tweet

definitions.meaning: a small high cry, like a bird's tweet

explanation.definitionFit: Both a furtive glance and the cheep of a young bird share this single word.

clue.text: Fine military vehicle's carrying king's opinion-makers

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the royal letter goes inside

parts.note: fine thread or hair is thin
tanks are armoured military vehicles; the 's makes the plural reading
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fine tank has room for the king, who has strong opinions of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is the container: the two-part outer word holds the king between its halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Think tanks are research institutes that shape policy and public debate, so they make opinions.
